\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ચશ્માં} (caśmā̃)}{ચશ્માં (caśmā̃)}]{\gu{ચશ્માં} (caśmā̃) — glasses, spectacles}

\label{lesson:GU-C88-glasses}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a cap, then the Gujarati for an umbrella.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ચશ્માં}}
\textbf{\gu{ચશ્માં}} (\emph{caśmā̃}) — \textquotedblleft{}glasses, spectacles\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ચશ્માં}} (\emph{caśmāṁ}) is a loan, usually traced to Persian \emph{chashma}, \textquotedblleft{}spring, fountain\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{chashm}, \textquotedblleft{}eye\textquotedblright{}. The sense \textquotedblleft{}spectacles\textquotedblright{} grew up in India.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for glasses, bag, wallet, letter, gift.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{caśmā̃}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{caśmā̃}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{caśmā̃}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a cap, then the Gujarati for an umbrella, then say \emph{caśmā̃} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ચશ્માં} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Glasses, spectacles\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
